question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 6 & 2 \\ 2 & 8 & 2 \\ 6 & 2 & 8\end{bmatrix}$. Decompose $A$ into the sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix. Verify your answer by explicitly checking the symmetry/skew-symmetry.
explanation:
A symmetric matrix $S = \frac{1}{2}(A+A')$ and skew-symmetric matrix $K = \frac{1}{2}(A-A')$.
First compute transpose:
$A' = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 & 6 \\ 6 & 8 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 8\end{bmatrix}$

$A+A' = \begin{bmatrix}8 & 8 & 8 \\ 8 & 16 & 4 \\ 8 & 4 & 16\end{bmatrix}$
$A-A' = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 4 & -4 \\ -4 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}$

$S = \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}8 & 8 & 8 \\ 8 & 16 & 4 \\ 8 & 4 & 16\end{bmatrix}$
$= \begin{bmatrix}4 & 4 & 4 \\ 4 & 8 & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & 8\end{bmatrix}$

$K = \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 & 4 & -4 \\ -4 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}$
$= \begin{bmatrix}0 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}$

Check symmetry:
$S' = S$ so $S$ is symmetric.
Check skew symmetry:
$K' = -K$ so $K$ is skew-symmetric.
Thus $A = S + K$.
